A1.name: OCR drops or mangles whole lines
A1.lesson: Recall is measured against OCR itself, so lost lines are invisible. Add an independent check: text lines in the page image (ink rows) with no OCR words; a second OCR model on pages where the first leaves gaps; flag pages whose OCR word count is far below the page's ink.

A2.name: A scanner's OCR layer passes for real text
A2.lesson: A page under one full-page image is a scan whatever its layer says: route as scanner_ocr, compare with independent OCR, treat agreement < 0.9 as suspect (8,108 such pages classed digital; 2,350 with agreement < 0.9).

A3.name: Handwriting, stamps and signatures read as words
A3.lesson: Keep OCR text from pictures classed signature/stamp and from handwriting out of the body (keep it in the evidence); never make it a heading.

A4.name: Graphic marks read as characters (logos, symbols, check marks)
A4.lesson: Treat an OCR word that is a lone CJK character (or a lone mark) in a Latin-script page or inside a picture as a symbol, not text; keep runs of CJK (real Chinese exists: 4105885). Never let OCR-only words into text-layer sentences on digital pages.

B1.name: Wrong characters behind right-looking glyphs
B1.lesson: Compare digits and words with OCR on a sample of every digital document; a layer that disagrees is suspect even if it decodes to 'words'. Decode known offsets only where OCR agrees. Map known substitutions (U+0BD7 for U+202F in Justice Canada French; U+FFFD runs as leaders).

examples.output_says: P-value o0.001, P-value o0.05 (in the text layer itself)

drawing; whole word shifted by a fixed offset in the text layer

B2.name: Symbol fonts: bullets and check boxes as letters
B2.lesson: Map Wingdings/Symbol characters by font name before export (þ→☑, ¨→☐, private-use bullets → •); write a check box's option once, with its state. Never drop a private-use code point silently: the degree sign stored as U+F0B0 is deleted today (4334400: '100 °F' becomes '100 F'); map Symbol's U+F0xx range to Unicode (U+F0B0 → °, U+F0B1 → ±, U+F0B7 → •).

examples.page_shows: Corrosion, Copper Strip at 100 °F (degree sign in a symbol font)

B3.name: Words broken or run together by spacing
B3.lesson: Join single letters spaced at a regular pitch into words; join split words using the dictionary and the gap size; never trust a space narrower than the font's word space.

B4.lesson: Drop a glyph run that repeats the same text at (almost) the same position; keep one copy.

C1.name: The answer is a picture or a widget, not text
C1.lesson: Attach a small icon picture (check mark) to the text line it sits on and mark that option chosen, the others not; read AcroForm widget values (radio buttons) into the output.

D1.lesson: A bold lead-in whose baseline equals the first line of the text beside it is part of that paragraph, read first; never a heading. Affects ~56% of 17,026 orders.

E1.name: Numbered paragraphs become headings
E1.lesson: A bookmark or numbered line that is a sentence (over ~20 words, or ends with . ... ;) is a numbered paragraph; keep only short bookmarks as headings. 19.8% of Arguments, 8.5% of Written Evidence.

E2.name: Headings that are not on the page
E2.lesson: Never make a heading from a file name, a stamp, a signature rule (______) or an attachment label. A bookmark that matches no line on its page is not a heading: today it is anchored at the page's first element and written as one (merged PDFs point every sub-file's bookmarks at page 1). Take headings only from text drawn on the page.

E3.name: List numbers and bullets kept as text
E3.lesson: When a list item's text starts with its own marker (1., (a), •, -), drop the Markdown bullet and keep the marker (or emit an ordered list).

E4.name: Footnote markers fused to words; hyphens kept at line ends
E4.lesson: Mark superscript footnote references ([^22]); join a lower-case word broken at a line-end hyphen (not digit groups, not real compounds).

F1.name: A table over several pages filed under its first page
F1.lesson: Write each page's rows under that page's marker (repeat the header, mark it continued). 5.2% of substantial pages have most of their words under another page.

examples.page_shows: Peguis First Nation comment and response

F2.name: A table's own row numbers taken for margin numbering
F2.lesson: Never take line numbers from words inside a table region or a ruled column; keep the margin rule for prose with numbers outside the text block.

F3.name: A dense numeric table collapses into a column in one cell
F3.lesson: A cell whose words sit on several text-layer lines with one number each is several rows: rebuild the grid from the ruling lines there.

examples.output_says: one cell: (c) 0.1035 1.6473 0.5986 ...; paths as plain lines

F4.name: Cells shifted, split or merged
F4.lesson: Score grids against the ruling lines and the header count; reject grids with mostly empty columns.

examples.note: readings shifted one time-step; not image-checked

F5.name: A table's units and notes not attached to its numbers
F5.lesson: Carry caption, units, notes, footnotes and the header path on every table and cell.

G1.name: Drawings, maps and charts: labels without order or relation
G1.lesson: Do not attempt reading order; keep labels findable with their boxes; never present them as prose.

H1.name: Bilingual side-by-side text read across both languages
H1.lesson: Detect the two-language column layout and emit each column whole.

I1.name: Pictures misclassified or repeated
I1.lesson: Merge overlapping picture regions before export (one logo was 4 regions); low-confidence classes should say 'picture'.

E5.name: Superscripts and subscripts flattened into the text (footnote marks into numbers, exponents, units)
E5.lesson: Emit superscript/subscript runs as such (^4, <sup>), and footnote references as references; never concatenate a raised digit to the number before it. Flag cells where a number ends in a raised digit.

candidates.name: Access-to-information redaction marks read as numbers; redacted text left as a silent gap
candidates.page_shows: Exemption stamps 's.17' and 's.19(1)' at top right, and a blanked-out name in 'We should involve [redacted] as well in this'
candidates.output_says: 5.17 / 5.19(1) ... We should involvi as well in this, as he is the Project Engineer
candidates.why_it_matters: The stamps become bare numbers with no sign they are legal exemption marks; the sentence reads as complete though a name was withheld, and the output does not say anything was redacted or on what ground
candidates.lesson: Detect exemption stamps (s.NN) and blanked regions, emit an explicit [redacted: s.19(1)] marker so withheld text is not mistaken for missing or complete text

candidates.name: Handwritten overwrite turns a typed identifier into a different valid-looking one
candidates.page_shows: Typed 'GH-003-2018' with a handwritten scribble over the final digits, and 'Round 3' with a handwritten 3 written over the typed 3; the cc line below reads GH-003-2018
candidates.output_says: Hearing Order GH-003-2013NOVA Gas Transmission Ltd. ... submit Round Information Requests
candidates.why_it_matters: The hearing order number is the key a filing is indexed and cited by; it now reads as a different, real-looking hearing (2013), run into the next word, and the round number is gone. Nothing flags it, and the cc line contradicts it.
candidates.lesson: Cross-check identifiers inside a document (subject vs cc line vs metadata) and flag disagreements; filers should not overwrite typed text by hand.

candidates.name: Rotated column headers read with words in scrambled order
candidates.page_shows: Vertical column headers 'Segment Unique ID', 'Wetland Unique ID', 'Distance of Wetland from Access Road (m)'
candidates.output_says: | Segment ID Unique | ... | ID Wetland Unique | ... | of from Road Distance Wetland Access (m) |
candidates.why_it_matters: Header labels become word salad, so a column cannot be matched to a field name; 'ID Wetland Unique' vs 'Unique ID' breaks field search and any schema inference over the table
candidates.lesson: Detect rotated (90 degree) text and read each header cell as one line in its rotated direction; do not sort words by horizontal position

candidates.page_shows: Notes block with 'EXCAVATION NOTE: TRENCH SHORING WILL BE USED IF PROPER TRENCH EXCAVATION CAN NOT BE USED', 'VERTICAL DATUM: CANADIAN GEODETIC VERTICAL DATUM 1928 (78 ADJ).', distance-to-feet note, and the first 'THE UTILITY DATA ... ASCE STANDARD 38-02' lines; the PDF text layer holds all of them

candidates.why_it_matters: safety and datum notes (trench shoring, vertical datum, utility quality level A) are silently gone, replaced by 2-4 letter fragments that look like text; word-count checks pass; search for 'shoring' finds nothing
candidates.lesson: drawing sheets with small vector text: text-layer lines that overlap table/figure regions are being discarded by region assignment; fall back to the PDF text layer for any word not emitted, and flag fragments of fewer than 4 letters

candidates.name: Gantt bar labels and overlay line merged into table rows as garbled dates
candidates.page_shows: A schedule table on the left and a Gantt chart on the right; the bars carry date labels (e.g. 11-May-23 ... 18-May-23) and a red data-date line runs through them. Table Current Finish for the row is 18-May-23.
candidates.why_it_matters: The chart's own labels are read as extra table columns, truncated at the chart edge, and the line through them changes digits: 18-May-23 becomes a valid-looking 18-May-21 (two years earlier), other dates become nonsense. A scheduling query over the table gets wrong dates with nothing to mark them as chart annotations.
candidates.lesson: Treat the Gantt area as a chart region: do not OCR it into table cells; keep only the table columns, or flag the chart as a picture with its labels unattached.

candidates.name: Zero shown as a dash is dropped, leaving an empty cell
candidates.page_shows: Rows such as Materials & Supplies, Transmission Line Pack, Prepayments, Other each show '$ -' (zero) in the Initial Annual Forecast column, and the Deferrals row '$ -'.
candidates.output_says: | Materials & Supplies | Input |  |  |  |  and  | Deferrals (as Applicable) |  |  |  | $ |
candidates.why_it_matters: A reported zero becomes an empty cell, indistinguishable from 'not reported'; the dollar sign alone survives on some rows and not others, so sums and checks (Total Working Capital = Sum L5 to L9) cannot be followed and zero vs missing is lost. The OCR keeps '$' but not the dash.
candidates.lesson: Keep dash placeholders as an explicit value (0 or '-') with its row; flag cells where only a currency sign was read.
